page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E6.256 is a dedicated bare-metal cloud instance engineered for high-density compute and memory requirements. Built on the x86_64 processor architecture, the physical machine is powered by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system provides 256 physical cores running 2 threads per core, yielding 512 dedicated vCPUs with direct hardware execution free from hypervisor overhead. System memory totals 3072 GB, providing an allocation of 6.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is addressed through an onboard 1920 GB NVMe solid-state drive, and external connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Hardware capabilities prioritize multi-core parallelism and large contiguous memory allocation over graphical acceleration, as the platform does not feature GPU coprocessors. Dedicated physical access ensures predictable execution cycles without noisy-neighbor contention across all 512 logical execution threads. While the bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD delivers low-latency IO operations suitable for operating system duties, temporary scratchpads, and caching layers, primary persistent data storage for massive workloads typically relies on network-attached block volumes given the modest local drive capacity relative to the multi-terabyte memory envelope.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform consolidates massive computing footprints into a single bare-metal chassis, reducing system orchestration complexity and per-node licensing overhead compared to managing several smaller virtual machines. The architectural balance of compute density and extensive memory capacity renders BM.Standard.E6.256 suitable for high-throughput batch processing, distributed data analytics pipelines, large-scale in-memory databases, extensive virtualization hypervisors, and container orchestration clusters handling substantial concurrent connection loads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard.E6.256 is a dedicated bare-metal server built on the x86_64 architecture for high-capacity enterprise workloads. The hardware profile comprises 256 physical cores and 512 vCPUs driven by AMD EPYC 9J45 processors running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. It provides 3072 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and integrates a 1920 GB local NVMe SSD for fast auxiliary storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. Operating without a virtualization hypervisor layer or GPU accelerators, the server delivers raw compute density across all physical processor sockets. From an infrastructure cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU and RAM density consolidates extensive multi-threaded computing into a single bare-metal deployment. This configuration is engineered for large-scale enterprise deployments, distributed container nodes, extensive relational and in-memory databases, and batch computing pipelines requiring massive thread parallelization.
